headline: Medium pairwise risk: Pipecat’s shared-bus, networked voice pipeline can amplify prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors when paired with Pathway’s document-processing outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pathway has no direct output channel to Pipecat, but Pipecat’s shared bus and stdin/stdout surfaces can bridge content into a voice pipeline. If Pathway-produced text is forwarded into Pipecat without filtering, Pipecat may treat it as conversational input or instructions. The pathway is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF Pathway outputs are forwarded into Pipecat via stdin/stdout or a shared bus
IF Pipecat parses forwarded text as conversational content or tool instructions
mitigations: Add an explicit content separator and provenance tag before forwarding text
Disable automatic instruction-following on forwarded documents
Route Pathway output through a sanitizer that strips imperative phrases
Use a one-way transform that converts documents to plain summaries
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pathway is document-processing and Pipecat touches text, conversation state, and analytics/metrics while also calling external APIs by default. If Pathway handles sensitive documents and those contents are passed into Pipecat, the pair can leak data to third-party STT/LLM/TTS services. This is a default-path concern for Pipecat; Pathway’s local-only profile does not block the handoff.
conditions: IF any Pathway text is sent into Pipecat services that call external APIs
IF Pipecat logging or analytics captures conversation state containing that text
mitigations: Redact sensitive fields before handoff
Disable analytics/telemetry for the session
Use local-only STT/LLM/TTS backends where available
Restrict the shared bus to non-sensitive summaries
requires-engineering: enforce data-class routing policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pathway cannot write files or use network egress, so it has little direct write conflict with Pipecat. Pipecat supports shared-bus session state and multiple instances, which can create contention if the orchestrator multiplexes both agents onto the same mutable channel. The overlap is limited because Pathway lacks write and modify capabilities.
conditions: IF both agents are attached to the same mutable bus or workspace
IF the orchestrator does not serialize writes to shared session state
mitigations: Assign separate session IDs per agent
Serialize writes through a single coordinator
Avoid shared mutable files for inter-agent exchange
Use read-only handoff artifacts
requires-engineering: add locking around shared bus updates

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat can consume text and conversation state from upstream components, so Pathway outputs may become authoritative inputs if the orchestrator wires them together. Because Pipecat also invokes LLM/STT/TTS services, an error in Pathway can cascade into spoken or acted-upon outputs. The interaction is inferred from documented interfaces rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Pathway-generated text is used as Pipecat input without verification
IF Pipecat downstream services render or act on that text
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Pipecat consumes Pathway output
Require human review for high-impact outputs
Attach confidence metadata to Pathway results
Block automatic action-taking on unverified text
requires-engineering: implement schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, so only a limited compliance concern is visible. Pipecat’s analytics/metrics and external API integrations can create policy obligations if Pathway processes regulated documents, but the profiles do not show a concrete cross-border or certification conflict. Pathway is not cited for the missing compliance dimensions because they are absent, not contradictory.
conditions: IF regulated data processed by Pathway is forwarded into Pipecat
IF Pipecat telemetry or third-party services retain that data beyond policy limits
mitigations: Disable telemetry for regulated sessions
Keep regulated documents out of Pipecat inputs
Review vendor DPAs before deployment
Set short retention on logs and transcripts
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
